title: Direction
description: One provider-neutral creative document: who is in frame, what they want, where they stand, how the camera watches them, what the light does. It is not a prompt. It names entities (cast ids); a renderer turns them into the target model's own addressing and dialect. A field exists only when some renderer treats it differently from another. Platform parameters (duration, resolution, aspect, tier, seed) and prompt syntax (@Image1, section headers, timecodes) are deliberately absent. The document carries direction_version; version 1 stays readable, version 2 additionally requires every scripted line to name a cast owner.

direction_version.description: Schema version of this document; 2 today. Required on the wire: it is how a Direction is told apart from other JSON. Bumped only when a field's meaning changes in a way a stored Direction cannot survive; additive fields do not bump it. A reader keeps accepting older versions.

cast.description: Every addressable entity: people, places, props, vehicles, styles. Ids are unique within the list; the reference reader refuses a repeat, which this schema cannot say.

performance.description: Behaviour per character. A performance for someone not in cast is an authoring error a renderer surfaces.

shots.description: One shot is a single take; more than one is a controlled multi-shot sequence with explicit cuts.

continuity.description: What must not change across an internal cut. Only meaningful with more than one shot.

storyboard.description: Optional server-defined block. Its fields are documented by the hosted service.

$comment: This schema describes the canonical form of a Direction. The reference reader tolerates the spellings AI hosts write: before it validates, it folds case, spaces and hyphens in enum values and maps a few synonyms onto them (Mid-ground, MIDDLE GROUND or mid become midground). That normalisation is a documented pre-validation step, not part of the contract: a writer emits the canonical spelling, and a port that wants the same tolerance applies the same step first. The reference implementation exposes it as canonical_direction, which returns the normalised document; the document it returns validates against this schema. Scalars are strict: the string '4.5' is not a number, 1 is not a boolean and true is not a number. Not expressible in JSON Schema, and enforced by the reference reader: from version 2 every audio.dialogue[].who must equal the id of a cast member (the schema only requires a non-empty who); cast ids are unique (the schema cannot require uniqueness by one key); and a beat may not both activate and suppress the same facial action at the same timing and laterality (see beat).

intent.title: Intent
intent.description: What the author asked for, kept verbatim. A renderer never discards or paraphrases line; it is the last thing cut for length.

cast_member.title: Cast member
cast_member.description: One addressable entity. Places are cast members too: a location reference steers a shot the way a character sheet steers a face.

id.description: Stable id other parts of the Direction point at.

name.description: Display name for prose. Falls back to id.

binding.description: Which wired reference this entity is, addressed generically as '<kind>#<index>' where kind is image, video or audio and index is 0-based in wire order (image#0, video#1). Empty means described but not referenced. The reference reader does not check the form; a renderer reads it.

reference_role.description: Semantic job of the bound reference: camera_motion marks a grey-box camera previz that must not be read as appearance.

anchors.description: The minimum critical anchors for the shot: age, role, state, unique visible identifiers.

locked.description: True when the anchors sentence was confirmed against a generated reference sheet and must be reproduced verbatim.

blocking_entry.title: Blocking entry
blocking_entry.description: Where one cast member is and where they are pointed. Body direction and gaze are separate facts.

anchor.description: A measured landmark (within 1 meter of the burned car), not a vague one.

gaze_target.description: What they look at and where it is, including the camera relationship.

movement.description: Where the body goes, including when it goes nowhere.

staging.title: Staging
staging.description: The frame's geography and what is in it when it opens.

spatial_compass.description: A sealed coordinate system for coverage: named landmarks, their screen relationship, the camera side of the 180-degree line.

first_frame.description: Cast ids that must be visible in frame one.

proxemics.description: Distance between people, and where it changes.

facial_action.title: Facial action
facial_action.description: One anatomically observable facial action (a FACS Action Unit), not an emotion label. Stored as provenance and lowered to observable English before any dialect renders it.
facial_action.$comment: The allOf rules restate the reference reader's coherence checks: an activated action needs a visible intensity, a suppressed one must use none, AU17 is a central chin action and stays bilateral, a baseline action must hold through a beat or shot, an offset action cannot be held. A suppress action must name intensity none explicitly, because its default (slight) is not none.

beat.title: Beat
beat.description: The smallest unit of action: one want, pursued one way. A beat ends when the objective lands, the tactic fails, new information arrives or the power balance shifts, and the change must be visible.

shot_id.description: Optional id of the Shot this beat belongs to. Empty keeps chronological distribution.

beat.$comment: Not expressible: within one beat two facial actions with the same au, laterality and timing must not disagree on mode (activate against suppress). The reference reader refuses it. A shot-held facial action requires a shot_id with a non-blank character, as checked here.

performance.title: Performance
performance.description: One character's behaviour under pressure. Emotion is deliberately not a field: a character wants something, something is in the way, and they act.

objective.description: A verb aimed at a partner, never a state.

body.description: Centre of gravity, tempo, openness, breath as one prose line.

business.description: The physical task the character does while talking.

voice.description: A locked vocal identity, reproduced verbatim where the dialect has a place for it.

optics.title: Optics
optics.description: Lens character expressed as an observable outcome, not as metadata.

fov_deg.description: Field of view in whole degrees. The canonical ladder is 8, 18, 29, 47, 84, 107; the reference reader accepts any integer.

outcome.description: Observable phrases that hold the lens against drift.

camera.title: Camera
camera.description: Where the operator stands and how the camera moves.

shot.title: Shot
shot.description: One continuous camera position. Every cut is explicit because an unspecified cut is an invented one.

camera.description: Shot-local operator state; null means the Direction's camera applies.

optics.description: Per-shot lens override; null means the Direction's optics.

who.description: A cast id. From direction_version 2 it must be non-empty and name a cast member.

audio.title: Audio
audio.$comment: music must be blank when music_policy is none, and must contain a non-blank character when it is authored. Blank means whitespace only, as in the reference reader's strip().

edit_intent.title: Edit intent
edit_intent.description: Present when the Direction edits an existing image or clip rather than generating one.

guard.title: Guard
guard.description: Something that must not happen, with the positive thing to do instead.
